belief: Jesus saved me, but now it’s up to me to stay acceptable.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that after salvation it is up to you to stay acceptable to God, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Hearing that grace saves you, but then being judged by rules, attendance, and appearance. A parent whose love depended on good behavior. Sermons that stress effort and duty more than God’s faithfulness. Repeated struggles with the same sin, which seem to prove you are slipping. A perfectionistic personality that keeps score.
teaches: You did not earn God’s acceptance at the start, and you do not keep it by your own effort now. The same grace that saved you holds you. Christ has already made you holy and blameless in God’s sight, and God Himself promises to finish the work He began in you. Your obedience matters, but it is a grateful response to His love, not the price of keeping it.
self_statements: One more slip and God will be done with me.
I have to keep proving I’m really saved.
Grace got me in, but now it’s all on me.
I’m only as acceptable as my last good day.
If I stop trying hard, God will pull away.
I have to make up for my failures.
errors: “I should be perfect by now,” as if God’s acceptance depends on it.
Believing you are either fully keeping up or completely falling away.
Making yourself responsible for what only Christ can do: keep you.
Focusing on your failures while ignoring God’s promises to hold you.
Predicting that God will reject you if you fall short again.
questions: Did I earn God’s acceptance in the first place?
If grace started this, why would I have to finish it by effort?
Who does Scripture say will complete the good work in me?
Am I trying to obey out of love, or out of fear of losing God?
Has Christ made me blameless, or have I?
What would change if I believed God is holding me, not just watching me?
Is it possible I learned this from people, not from the Bible?
truth: Jesus saved me by grace, and He keeps me by grace. My acceptance rests on what Christ has done, not on how well I perform. God began a good work in me, and He will finish it. I obey because I am loved, not to stay loved.
hw_questions: Did I earn God’s acceptance in the first place?

hw_truths: Grace saved me, and grace keeps me.
God will finish the good work He started in me.
Christ has made me holy and blameless in God’s sight.
I obey because I am loved, not to stay loved.
My acceptance rests on Jesus, not on my performance.
God is able to keep me from stumbling.
log: Each day, write one way God showed me grace that I did not earn.
name_example: Being confident of this, that He who began a good work in Sarah will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
actions: Take a real day of rest
without doing anything “spiritual” to make up for it, and notice whether God feels farther away.
After a mistake, confess it once,
thank God for His forgiveness, and move on without extra penance.
Do one act of service from gratitude,
and tell no one about it.
“Do you think God keeps you, or do you keep yourself?” Write down their answer.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for saving me by grace and for holding me by grace. Help me reject the lie that it is now up to me to stay acceptable. When I fall short, remind me that You have made me blameless and that You will finish what You began. Let my obedience grow out of love, not fear. In Your name, Amen.
songs: Christ bears the burden of rescue rather than demanding self-salvation.
